coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Potrero Power Station Block 12
record.summary: Planned commercial block on the Potrero Power Station masterplan (the design guidelines permit office and laboratory/life-science uses), paired with Block 11 in the project engineer's description of about 430,000 sq ft of office with below-grade parking (the Planning Department's October 2020 Phase 1 approval lists about 177,000 sq ft of commercial space for Block 12 and 219,000 for Block 11, about 396,000 together; the sources differ and are not reconciled). Design was under review as of the March 2025 annual compliance report. In a request reported July 29, 2026, the developer asked to raise Block 12's height by 23 feet and let it become residential or commercial; the Planning Commission approved the amendment unanimously (reported Aug 3, 2026) and the Board of Supervisors passed the amended development agreement on first reading on Sept 29, 2026, and Legistar lists it enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Mayor 'APPROVED'); the enacted height map gives Block 12 123 ft, or 115 ft if majority non-residential (100 ft in the adopted rules), taking effect Nov 13, 2026 by our count. No construction start found.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 4232023, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. That this is the lot of Block 12 is Pier & Point's own inference from location, shape and size (our earlier trace of the D4D figure measured 2,940 m2 against the lot's 2,645 m2; 77% of the trace lies inside the lot and the trace covers 85% of it). No document read ties the lot number to it. A building may sit back from the lot lines. Block 12 is not yet built, which is consistent with the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025), which says vertical applications are under review for Blocks 11 and 12.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lot 4232023 (recorded 2022-08-30; mapped 2023-12-01; active); cross-checked against Potrero Power Station Design for Development Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No single Assessor lot is documented as Block 12. Lot 4232023 (active) matches its location, shape and size, so its outline is Assessor lot 4232023; the identification is Pier & Point's inference, as the accuracy note says.
notes.regulatory_context: Flat 100 ft max height per Figure 6.2.3. Paired with Block 11 on the project's MEP engineer's page (Meyers+), which describes the two blocks together as about 430,000 sq ft of office with below-grade parking (see that entry for the combined GSF estimate); the final D4D's Table 3.1.1 permits laboratory and life-science uses on Block 12, but no cited source calls the pair a life-science campus. No construction-start source found; the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025) says vertical applications for Blocks 11 and 12 were under review.

facts.value: Office and laboratory/life science permitted; residential not permitted in the adopted rules (a 2026 amendment, enacted Oct 13, 2026 per Legistar, would allow it; the final ordinances say 'This ordinance shall become effective on the 31st day after enactment', November 13, 2026 by our count, a legal date computed by us; the enacted use rules are not yet checked against this record)
100 ft until the 2026 amendment takes effect (adopted D4D, Figure 6.2.3)

open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 12; the most recent primary source found (the 2024 annual compliance report) describes design as 'under review', not approved.

The combined 430,000 sq ft figure for Blocks 11+12 comes from the project's MEP engineer (Meyers+). The Planning Department's October 7, 2020 Phase 1 approval lists approximately 177,000 sq ft of commercial space for Block 12 and 219,000 for Block 11 (about 396,000 together, plus PDR, retail and other uses); no source reconciles the two figures.

The Chronicle's July 2026 report of a proposed +23 ft height increase and added residential flexibility is tied to the Development Agreement and Planning Code amendment package (BOS Files 260724 and 260770), which passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 and finally on Oct 6, 2026 (11 ayes), and Legistar lists it enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Legistar: Mayor 'APPROVED'; enactment numbers 208-26 and 209-26; page read Oct 14, 2026). The enacted height map labels Block 12 "123'" with a 115 ft limit for a majority non-residential building (File 260770 'Leg Final' attachment, p. 29), the 23 ft the Chronicle reported, effective November 13, 2026 by our count (a legal date computed by Pier & Point, not printed in the text). The enacted use rules (residential on Block 12) have not yet been checked against this record, so its use fact still shows the adopted rule.

Whether Blocks 11 and 12 are described as a life-science campus anywhere: the Meyers+ page, which pairs them, describes about 430,000 sq ft of office (its list of uses for the wider project includes laboratory), and the 2024 annual compliance report treats them together in a single 'Blocks 11 and 12 Design Review Application' without calling them a life-science campus; the D4D permits laboratory/life-science use on Block 12, and the Chronicle (July 29, 2026) quotes developer Enrique Landa saying all commercial parcels can be 'all PDR, all offices, all life sciences or all labs', but no cited source says that is the plan for Block 12.

Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): the July 2026 Development Agreement amendment request was shown as an expected event after it had been made and heard; it is now shown as having happened, with the Planning Commission's unanimous approval (SF Standard, August 3, 2026). Update 2026-10-12: the Board of Supervisors passed the amendment package on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 (see milestones). Update 2026-10-17: Legistar lists the package as approved by the Mayor and enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Enactment Nos. 208-26 and 209-26; page read Oct 17, 2026); the Board's final passage on Oct 6, 2026 (Ayes: 11) is shown by the Clerk of the Board's certificate in each file's 'Leg Final' attachment (File 260724 attachment pp. 11-12; File 260770 attachment pp. 58-59), although the Legistar web page's 10/6/2026 history row carries no action text.
